1.explanation:
1. resources/filters/quarto-pre/layout.lua and html.lua   These Lua filters run before Reveal output and handle how generic Divs and inline HTML are transformed in the AST. They have explicit cases for known containers (callouts, columns, panels) but do not treat an arbitrary classed div as a real block wrapper. As a result, the markdown image element (which itself generates its own Para/Image block) gets floated out of the surrounding Div.  
2. resources/filters/quarto-post/reveal.lua   This post-filter unwraps certain nested Divs when assembling slides and sections. Because the custom div class isn’t recognized, its contents are flattened and the image moves outside.  
3. src/format/reveal/format-reveal.ts   This TypeScript driver wires up the Lua filters (in the wrong order or without including a catch-all for custom blocks) and calls Pandoc with them. It needs to be updated to pass through arbitrary Div containers so images and other block elements remain nested inside user-defined wrappers.
1.bug_scenario: The user wants to wrap an image (and some text) inside an arbitrary named div (e.g. {.qrcodeblock} or {.anotherblocks}), but after rendering to a Reveal.js presentation the image is being pushed outside of that div and rendered after the closing tag. In contrast, when the same markup is placed inside the built-in .columns/.column blocks, the image stays in place. The three screenshots show: (A) a custom .qrcodeblock where the image appears below the div; (B) a .columns layout where the image is correctly nested; and (C) a nested custom div (outer .anotherblocks + inner .qrcodeblockagain) where again the image slips out of the inner div.

2.explanation:
1. resources/filters/quarto-post/reveal.lua: This Lua filter runs after Pandoc and is responsible for converting Div blocks to <section> elements (slides) and for folding in content. It contains logic to unwrap or drop Divs with unrecognized classes — that logic is accidentally stripping out image paragraphs inside custom divs and pushing them outside of the wrapper.

2. src/format/reveal/format-reveal.ts: This TypeScript module sets up the Reveal format and hooks in the post-processing filters (including the above Lua filter). It also merges slide content into sections and carries over classes/attributes. Because reveal.lua is unwrapping custom Divs, format-reveal.ts never sees those wrappers to inject them into the final HTML. Fixing reveal.lua (or its registration in format-reveal.ts) will ensure custom div blocks retain their image children in place.
2.bug_scenario: In the RevealJS slides generated by Quarto, arbitrary divs (e.g. ::: {.qrcodeblock} or ::::.{.anotherblocks}) get “un-wrapped” when they contain an image: the paragraph text stays inside the <div> but the image paragraph gets lifted out and rendered after the block. Only the built-in columns syntax avoids that because it uses a special filter path. In short, custom block divs aren’t being emitted correctly by the Reveal post-processing filter, so images slip outside.
